source_name: Stavební spořitelna České spořitelny, a.s. („Buřinka“) – Výroční zprávy
why_relevant: Erste/Česká spořitelna's building society, still a separate licensed and separately audited entity (100% ČS-owned; historically 95% ČS / 5% Bausparkasse der österreichischen Sparkassen). Publishes an unusually deep annual-report archive covering 2000–2025 in three decade blocks, which makes it the best long-run series in the cell for tracking branch/advisor counts, product digitalisation and cost structure inside the Erste CZ group. Content is now hosted on the csas.cz subdomain while ČNB still points at burinka.cz.

source_name: MONETA Stavební Spořitelna, a.s. (ex-Wüstenrot) – Financial results / dceřiné společnosti
why_relevant: The only building society in the cell whose subsidiary-level disclosures are published inside a listed parent's IR site, in both Czech and English, with reports reported back to 2015 (under the former name Wüstenrot - stavební spořitelna a.s. until 3 July 2020). MONETA is exchange-listed, so the subsidiary numbers arrive on a disciplined IR calendar and can be reconciled against group results — the cleanest quantitative baseline for building-society channel economics in CZ.

source_name: AČSS – Asociace českých stavebních spořitelen
why_relevant: Trade body that has united all building societies on the Czech market since 2000 (currently five members — exactly this cell's building-society universe). Publishes sector aggregates that entity reports do not standardise: new contract counts, loan volumes, and a recurring 'Barometr obliby spoření' savings-preference survey. Useful as a cross-check on entity-level annual reports and as an early indicator of sector-wide product and distribution shifts; also runs a second consumer-facing domain.

source_name: ČSOB Penzijní společnost, a.s. (člen skupiny ČSOB) – Dokumenty
why_relevant: Pension arm of the KBC/ČSOB group, separately licensed and separately audited, with its own statutory reporting for the company and for each účastnický and transformovaný fond. Its documents expose how a bank group distributes and services a long-tail savings product — branch vs advisor vs digital enrolment, client-portal features, statement delivery — at an entity level the ČSOB consolidated report does not disaggregate.

source_name: KB Penzijní společnost, a.s. – Zprávy o hospodaření a fondové dokumenty
why_relevant: Komerční banka group's pension company, publishing a dedicated 'zprávy o hospodaření' series plus separate document sets for účastnické fondy and the transformovaný fond. Because KB is simultaneously collapsing Modrá pyramida into the bank, KB PS reporting is the control case for how the same group handles a second non-bank licensed subsidiary — whether it too is being pulled into KB+ servicing or kept at arm's length.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – penzijní společnost, a.s. – Ke stažení / Pro klienty
why_relevant: Erste/Česká spořitelna's pension company and the largest CZ third-pillar player by participants. Publishes full annual reports as PDFs on a stable path (a 2018 report is served from a csas.cz DAM path, showing group-wide document infrastructure). Paired with Buřinka, it lets the analysis compare two separately licensed ČS-group non-bank subsidiaries on the same channel and technology questions.

source_name: Generali penzijní společnost, a.s. – dokumenty a klíčové informace účastnických fondů
why_relevant: Successor to Penzijní společnost České pojišťovny and part of the Generali CEE financial group, which also owns a licensed investment company in CZ. Included because the cell needs at least one insurance-led (rather than bank-led) pension company as a counterfactual: its distribution mix is agent- and broker-heavy, so divergences from ČSOB PS / KB PS / ČS PS on servicing and self-service investment are diagnostic of bank-group strategy rather than product economics.

source_name: NN Penzijní společnost, a.s. – Zprávy o hospodaření
why_relevant: Second large non-bank pension company with a dedicated, well-labelled 'zprávy o hospodaření' archive and published účastnický-fond key information documents. Together with Generali it fixes the non-bank baseline against which bank-owned pension companies' channel and technology disclosures are compared, and its documents are among the easiest to parse in the pension segment.

source_name: APS ČR – Asociace penzijních společností ČR: čtvrtletní statistiky (data.apscr.cz)
why_relevant: Highest-value aggregator in the pension part of the cell and one of the most collectible sources found anywhere in this sweep. Covers all pension companies (8 members) quarterly across both systems (DPS and old PP), with participant numbers, assets under management, average contributions, pre-retiree counts, employer contributions, per-fund asset structure, and — critically for source mapping — shareholder structure, auditors, depositaries and portfolio managers for each fund. Files sit on a predictable https://data.apscr.cz/{YYYY}/Q{n}/{report}.pdf path, plus long-run 1995–2025 performance series.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR – III. pilíř: Základní ukazatele vývoje penzijního připojištění a DPS; Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu
why_relevant: Government-side counterpart to APS ČR: quarterly 'Základní ukazatele' releases with commentary, built from data pension companies report to MF, covering active contract counts and state-contribution volumes — the definitive denominator for third-pillar market sizing (e.g. ~4.2m active contracts at 31.12.2023). The annual 'Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu' additionally sets building societies, credit unions, pension companies and investment firms in one narrative with policy direction, which is where legislative pressure on these entities first becomes visible.

source_name: Patria Finance, a.s. (koncern ČSOB) – O Patria Finance / povinně zveřejňované informace a výroční zprávy
why_relevant: The clearest case of an investment firm inside a banking group in CZ: a licensed obchodník s cennými papíry, ČNB-supervised, part of the ČSOB concern since 1 January 2015, serving ~90k clients with ~CZK 140bn in assets across CZ, SK and HU. Its standalone annual reports are served from a stable CDN path and describe its own trading applications and platform development — direct evidence of in-group technology build vs buy that never appears in ČSOB's consolidated report.

source_name: ČSOB Asset Management, a.s. – Informační povinnost správce fondu
why_relevant: Licensed investiční společnost inside the ČSOB/KBC group and the second in-group non-bank entity (with Patria Finance) whose statutory reporting covers the same client base as ČSOB's branches. Fund-manager disclosure obligations mean per-fund reports plus company reporting, giving a view of how investment products are distributed through bank channels and how much of that has moved to digital/self-service.

source_name: Amundi Czech Republic (investiční společnost, a.s. a Asset Management, a.s.) – Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: Amundi runs two separately licensed CZ entities — an investiční společnost and an asset-management obchodník s cennými papíry — both indexed by ČNB, and is the asset-management arm of a European banking group (Crédit Agricole) distributing heavily through Czech bank branches. Its CZ statutory filings are the best available read on bank-branch-distributed fund flows from a manager that is not itself owned by the distributing bank.

source_name: Generali Investments CEE, investiční společnost, a.s. – Informační povinnost
why_relevant: Licensed investiční společnost inside the Generali CEE financial group, sister to Generali penzijní společnost. Because Generali CEE runs bank-like distribution partnerships in CZ without owning a bank, its entity filings isolate the cost and channel profile of fund manufacture from bank-owned distribution — a useful decomposition when reading ČSOB AM or ČS-group equivalents.

source_name: ČNB – Zpráva o výkonu dohledu nad finančním trhem (annual)
why_relevant: Annual supervisory report that counts and characterises the exact populations in this cell — banks including building societies, spořitelní a úvěrní družstva, pension companies and their funds, investment firms — and records licence grants, withdrawals, mergers and enforcement. It is the single best instrument for detecting that an entity in the cell has stopped existing or changed group affiliation, and for validating the completeness of any entity list assembled from disclosure indexes. Long PDF back-series (at least 2008 onward) enables consistent historical entity counts.

source_name: Garanční systém finančního trhu (Fond pojištění vkladů, Fond pro řešení krize)
why_relevant: Statutory deposit-guarantee and resolution-funding body to which every CZ-headquartered bank, building society and credit union must contribute by law. Its participant lists and contribution data provide an independent, exhaustive census of exactly the deposit-taking half of this cell, and its disclosures reveal failures and payouts (historically the main event risk for credit unions). It also issues bonds with base prospectuses, adding a further disclosure stream.

source_name: AKAT ČR – Asociace pro kapitálový trh: statistiky správců aktiv a tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: Trade body covering investment companies, asset managers, obchodníci s cennými papíry and banks operating on the CZ capital market — i.e. the investment-firm portion of this cell. Publishes quarterly aggregate AUM statistics (e.g. CZK 3.16tn entrusted to asset managers at 31.12.2024) broken down by manager and product type, providing the sector denominator that individual investment-firm annual reports lack. Press-release PDFs are often mirrored by member firms, giving alternate retrieval paths when the association site is awkward.

source_name: Stavebky.cz a Hypoindex.cz – odborný tisk ke stavebnímu spoření
why_relevant: Czech specialist trade press covering the building-society segment continuously, including annual 'jak si vedly stavební spořitelny' reviews, rate and tariff comparisons across all five societies, and coverage of distribution changes. Valuable as an early-warning and dating layer: rate moves, product withdrawals and branch/advisor changes appear here weeks or months before they are formalised in a výroční zpráva, and articles frequently cite the underlying entity documents, acting as a pointer.

source_name: Družstevnízáložny.cz / Fintimes.cz / Peníze.cz – přehledy družstevních záložen a stavebních spořitelen
why_relevant: Third-party directories that enumerate CZ credit unions and building societies with profile pages, and that surfaced entities and historical names (WPB Capital, Prague Credit Union, DZ NOVA, Moravský peněžní ústav lineage) not visible on ČNB's current index of six active credit unions. Useful strictly as a snowballing aid for historical entity names and for cross-checking that the regulator-derived list is complete; every fact taken from here must be re-verified against JERRS or Sbírka listin.

source_name: Národní rozvojová banka (NRB) — Výroční zprávy / "Veškeré informace o hospodaření naší banky"
why_relevant: Primary, uninterrupted annual-report archive (observed listing spanning 2002-2025) of the Czech national promotional bank. Reports disclose guarantee and loan programme volumes, number of approved cases, programme names (Expanze, Záruka, ENERG, Nová energetická úspora), partner commercial banks acting as on-lending intermediaries, subsidiary structure (NRB Investiční, and post-2024/2025 Česká exportní banka as subsidiary), and audited financials. Because NRB channels support through partner banks, its reports name commercial-bank counterparties, which is exactly the co-financier mapping this cell must deliver.

source_name: NRB — Novinky (press releases / news)
why_relevant: Continuous-flow announcements of new programme launches, ministry co-funded instruments (e.g. joint MŽP zero-interest loan programme), record volumes, tender intentions and organisational change. Fills the 11-month gap between annual reports and is the earliest public signal of new lending/guarantee programmes that commercial banks will distribute.

source_name: NRB — English section (About the Bank, Annual Report / Annual Review)
why_relevant: English-language mirror giving the national promotional bank's mission pillars, product taxonomy (guarantees, loans, equity/quasi-equity) and at least some English annual reports/reviews. Useful for cross-country normalisation of programme terminology and for citing to non-Czech-reading stakeholders.

source_name: NRB — Veřejné zakázky (public procurement) + contracting-authority profiles (TenderArena, NEN)
why_relevant: NRB is a contracting authority under Act 134/2016 Sb., so its IT, core-banking, card/payment and facility tenders are published. This is the procurement-relevant operating detail the cell rationale calls for: it reveals technology suppliers, contract values and renewal cycles at a state bank. Two profiles observed (GORDION legacy, TenderArena current) plus an NEN profile under the legacy CMZRB code.

source_name: Česká exportní banka (ČEB) — Výroční zprávy archive
why_relevant: Complete audited annual/consolidated financial reports observed for 2012-2025, each as a direct PDF, with HTML (ESEF-style) versions for recent years. ČEB is the state export bank and a lender alongside commercial banks on export deals; its reports carry new-business volumes (e.g. CZK 9.54bn new business in 2025), pre-tax profit, exposure geography and the EGAP insurance linkage. Since ČEB is being integrated as a subsidiary of NRB, this archive is also the evidentiary trail for the restructuring.

source_name: ČEB — Povinně zveřejňované informace + Veřejné zakázky a výběrová řízení
why_relevant: Statutory disclosure hub for the state export bank (FOI-regime information, prudential disclosures) plus a separate tender/selection-procedure page. Same dual value as NRB: financial disclosure plus supplier-side procurement intelligence for a state-owned bank.

source_name: ČEB — Novinky (press releases) and English site
why_relevant: Results announcements ahead of the annual report (e.g. record profit, new-business totals) and deal-level export financing news that names client exporters and partner banks. An English section exists at /en/ for cross-language citation.

source_name: EGAP (Exportní garanční a pojišťovací společnost) — Výroční zprávy archive 2003-2025
why_relevant: Deepest single-entity archive found in this cell: annual reports for every year 2003-2025 (2009 has both standalone and consolidated versions). EGAP is the state export credit insurer under Act 58/1995 Sb.; its reports carry insured-export volumes, claims, technical provisions, profit, country exposure and — critically for counterparty mapping — the commercial banks whose export financing EGAP insures.

source_name: EGAP — English section (Annual Reports, Profile, EGAP in numbers)
why_relevant: English mirror of the export credit agency including an annual-reports page, an identification-data page and an 'EGAP in numbers' summary. Enables comparison with peer ECAs (KUKE, SACE, EKN) without Czech-language parsing.

source_name: EGAP — Tiskové zprávy / aktuality (press releases, pricing and Ukraine Fund announcements)
why_relevant: EGAP publishes results and product news via press releases that are widely re-syndicated (ČTK/ČeskéNoviny, Echo24, Novinky). Observed items include full-year insured-export volumes, profit, number of policies and destination countries, plus the 'Fond Ukrajina' sub-scheme and OECD-country premium repricing — all leading indicators of state-backed trade-finance capacity available to Czech banks.

source_name: Garanční systém finančního trhu (GSFT) — Dokumenty: výroční zprávy, rozpočty, rozpočtové výhledy, prospekty dluhopisů
why_relevant: Single richest page in this cell. Confirmed listings of: annual reports 2005-2025 on stable, guessable paths (/ke-stazeni/vyrocni-zpravy/vyrocni-zprava-YYYY.pdf); approved budgets 2020-2026; budget outlooks through 2027-2028; and base prospectuses for the bond programmes of BOTH the Deposit Insurance Fund (FPV) and the Crisis Resolution Fund (FŘK) for 2021-2025. The annual reports and budgets carry fund balances, contribution rates and the per-bank contribution base — i.e. the size of the Czech deposit-insurance and resolution safety net, and forward-looking fund build-up plans.

source_name: Česká národní banka — Výroční zprávy ČNB / CNB Annual Reports (cs + en)
why_relevant: The central bank's own annual report — explicitly named in this cell. Covers mandate, organisational structure, supervisory and currency operations, payment-system operation (CERTIS), cash cycle, IT programmes, headcount and audited financial statements. Full English mirror exists with stable PDF paths (vz_YYYY_en.pdf), which is unusual and valuable for this cell.

source_name: ČNB — Roční zpráva o výsledku hospodaření ČNB + Roční účetní závěrka (Financial Reports to the Chamber of Deputies)
why_relevant: Separate statutory financial-result report submitted to the Chamber of Deputies under the CNB Act, plus the standalone audited annual accounts (auditor observed as Ernst & Young Audit). Distinct from the general annual report: it is the document Parliament debates, and it isolates the CNB's loss/profit position, FX-reserve valuation effects and accumulated loss — a recurring Czech policy story.

source_name: ČNB — Veřejné zakázky / E-ZAK ČNB a Úřední deska
why_relevant: The central bank's own e-procurement system (E-ZAK) plus the cnb.cz procurement page and official notice board. Directly procurement-relevant: CNB tenders cover payment-system (CERTIS), cash-handling, registry/IT and security infrastructure — the clearest public window on central-bank technology spend and its incumbent suppliers. CNB IČO 48136450; a mirrored authority profile exists on vhodne-uverejneni.cz.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR — Majetkové účasti Ministerstva financí (monthly state-ownership register)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance's own ownership reporting — explicitly required by this cell. Observed as an approximately MONTHLY snapshot ('Majetkové účasti Ministerstva financí ke dni …'), archived from 2006 to 2026, listing every company in which MF exercises shareholder rights, with stake percentages. This is the authoritative register showing MF as sole shareholder of EGAP, and the ownership chain over ČEB/NRB. Companion series 'Akciové společnosti ovládané ČR (MF)' gives yearly consolidated views. Monthly cadence makes it a leading indicator of restructurings, transfers and disposals.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR — Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu / Report on Financial Market Developments (annual, cs + en)
why_relevant: MF's annual whole-of-market report covering banking, payments, insurance, capital markets and pensions, with structural data and stated policy direction. Published in both Czech and English with stable PDF attachments. It is the government-side counterpart to the CNB supervision report and the best single document for MF's view of where the Czech financial market is heading — including state-institution roles.

source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra — Výroční zprávy o činnosti finančního arbitra
why_relevant: Market-safety body squarely inside this cell: the statutory out-of-court dispute resolver for payment services, consumer credit, life insurance, FX and payment-account switching. Its annual report (legally required by 30 June each year) is the only public source that quantifies consumer disputes BY PROVIDER and BY PRODUCT — observed 15,446 proceedings in 2025 with an extraordinary surge in consumer-credit disputes. That is direct, attributable conduct-risk intelligence on named Czech banks and payment institutions. KFA is a state organisational unit funded within the MF budget chapter.

source_name: Garanční fond obchodníků s cennými papíry (GFO)
why_relevant: The second Czech investor-protection safety net alongside GSFT: the guarantee fund for securities dealers, paying 90% of unpaid client assets up to EUR 20,000 on CNB notification. It is the investor-compensation-scheme counterpart to deposit insurance, and completes the market-safety-body map for this cell. Member firms include banks with investment-services licences, so its member list and levy data cross-reference the banking sector.

source_name: Podpůrný a garanční rolnický a lesnický fond (PGRLF, a.s.) — výroční zprávy
why_relevant: The agricultural/forestry state guarantee and subsidised-credit institution — the sector-specific sibling of NRB, established by Government Resolution 337/1993 and registered 16.9.1993. Its annual reports quantify guarantee and interest-subsidy volumes (observed: 14,303 applications and >CZK 2.5bn in 2024) and, like NRB, it works through partner commercial banks, so its reports name the lending banks. Frequently missed by banking-only source maps.

source_name: Státní fond podpory investic (SFPI) — Výroční zprávy
why_relevant: State investment/housing support fund (IČO 70856788) providing subsidised loans to municipalities and public investors, and since 2024 also advisory services. A policy-financial institution that competes with and co-finances alongside commercial banks in the municipal-lending segment, and whose financial statements are additionally exposed through the state treasury MONITOR system.

source_name: MONITOR — Státní pokladna (monitor.statnipokladna.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance transparency portal exposing budget, balance-sheet and closing-account data for every state accounting unit, searchable by IČO, with drill-through. For the state-funded members of this cell (SFPI, Kancelář finančního arbitra, ministry chapters) it provides structured, comparable financial data years before or independently of any PDF annual report — useful when an entity's own reporting is thin or late.

source_name: Hlídač státu (hlidacstatu.cz) — aggregator + open API over contracts, tenders, subsidies
why_relevant: NGO aggregator that normalises Registr smluv, Věstník veřejných zakázek, subsidy registers and entity metadata into one searchable corpus with a documented public API (/api/v1/doc). It already maintains per-entity dashboards for the exact institutions in this cell (NRB IČO 44848943, ČNB IČO 48136450, SFPI 70856788), splitting contracts vs. tenders vs. other databases. Best practical entry point for programmatic collection and for discovering entities and suppliers we did not know to look for.

source_name: Poslanecká sněmovna PČR — sněmovní tisky a fulltext (parliamentary reports by EGAP, ČEB, ČNB)
why_relevant: Statutory reporting channel that produces documents NOT published on the institutions' own sites. EGAP reports to the Chamber of Deputies on its state-supported activity (observed as twice-yearly in EGAP's own description of its obligations); the CNB submits its financial-result report; and the MF submits information on export insurance and financing with state support under Act 58/1995 Sb. The accompanying budget-committee records and explanatory memoranda often contain forward-looking programme sizing and government intentions before any press release. A full-text search endpoint exists at fulltext.psp.cz.

source_name: Nejvyšší kontrolní úřad (NKÚ) — kontrolní závěry a tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: The Supreme Audit Office audits exactly the entities in this cell and publishes full audit conclusions as PDFs plus press releases. Confirmed historical coverage includes an audit of state ownership stakes in commercial companies (K15005), a 2011-era audit of ČEB and EGAP that found imprudent lending and breaches of the Banking Act across nine loans worth CZK 13.2bn, and a more recent audit finding the CNB manages its finances without material errors. NKÚ conclusions are the only public source that contradicts the institutions' own self-reporting, which makes them disproportionately valuable for credibility triangulation. NKÚ's audit mandate over export-support institutions is itself anchored in Act 58/1995 Sb. / Act 166/1993 Sb.

source_name: MPO — Finanční nástroje / Majetkové účasti státu (ministry co-owner and programme sponsor)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Industry and Trade is the programme sponsor behind most NRB financial instruments (Expanze - úvěry / záruky, Úspory energie, ENERG, Nová energetická úspora funded from OPTAK and the Modernisation Fund) and also maintains its own register of state ownership stakes where it exercises shareholder rights. It publishes programme calls, allocation sizes and the government decisions behind restructurings — the MPO press release announcing the government decision to integrate ČEB into NRB is a case in point. Serves as a pointer to programme documentation that NRB itself only summarises.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR — tiskové zprávy (press releases, cs) as the ownership-decision channel
why_relevant: MF exercises shareholder rights over EGAP and (via the ownership chain) the ČEB/NRB group, so its press feed is where ownership restructurings, capital injections, board appointments and legislative milestones surface first — observed items include the government decision to integrate ČEB and NRB, three separate stages of the Act on the National Development Bank passing through the Chamber of Deputies, and annual announcements on results of strategic state companies and compliance with remuneration principles.
